title: Preflight briefing for exec staff — checklist & action journal
body:
Purpose: quick, scannable preflight for Monday exec staff (weekly). Focus: unblock decisions, align org priorities, capture ownerable actions.

Topline prep (what I need before the room):
- Updated one-pager (2x slide text) summarizing: revenue delta this quarter, dedicated capacity pipeline status, and 3 production incidents with customer impact. I will draft bullet points and attach.
- Headline metrics: global QTD token spend vs. budget, mean p95 latency for hosted API last 7 days, Dedicated committed capacity utilization % — keep numbers short (3 bullets).
- Decision requests (explicit):
  1) Approve temporary increase to Dedicated burst pool (+10%) to cover 48h spike for ACME. Owner: infra ops. Deadline: EOD Tues.
  2) Prioritize on-call tracer for model rollout rollback automation (MVP) — allocate 1 engineer for 2 weeks. Owner: serving-runtime.
  3) Sign-off on privacy attestation template for Private customers. Owner: legal/product security.

Meeting flow (timeboxed):
- 0:00–0:05: Quick open (context + 3 bullets that matter) — I lead.
- 0:05–0:15: Metrics & flags — Jonah presents p95 latency and budget delta.
- 0:15–0:30: Decision 1 (Dedicated burst) — discussion + vote.
- 0:30–0:45: Risk roundtable (incidents, compliance, hiring) — 2 min per leader to call out escalations.
- 0:45–0:55: Ops roadmap sync (rollouts, automation) — Priya to outline resource ask.
- 0:55–1:00: Clear actions & owners — I recap, confirm owners and deadlines.

Warm-up lines / framing to use:
- "We have three items that determine whether we hit our near-term SLA and revenue targets — let's decide on the first two now."
- "If we don't allocate short-term burst capacity we'll risk churn with a top-10 customer; cost is contained to the 48-hour window."
- "I'm asking for a narrow MVP resource commitment, not full productization — 2 week runway to get rollback automation landed."

Key facts to surface (short bullets to copy into chat as needed):
- QTD token spend: $1.2M (vs budget $1.05M) — variance 14%.
- Hosted API p95 latency (last 7 days): 210ms (target 180ms) — top contributor: model kv-cache miss rate increased by 12%.
- Dedicated pool utilization (last 24h): 87% steady; burst capacity used 65% when enabled.
- Incident summary: Mar 6: degraded routing (5% error rate for 18m) — rollback applied; Mar 10: cache warmup regression (increased cold starts).

Open questions I expect:
- Who signs budget for temporary burst? (finance or exec?)
- Does legal need to re-review customer comms for the ACME escalation?
- Can infra guarantee a 48h increase without perturbing other customers?

Risks & mitigations (one-liners):
- Risk: burst allocation causes transient latency for other tenants. Mitigation: apply strict traffic shaping, enable regional fallback. Owner: SRE.
- Risk: rollback automation might miss edge-case model configs. Mitigation: schedule staged canary and manual guardrails. Owner: release-engineering.
- Risk: increased spend triggers finance alarm. Mitigation: prom threshold and auto-notify CFO. Owner: finance ops.

Action journal (pre-populate during meeting; transfer to tracker after):
- [ ] Approve Dedicated +10% burst for ACME (owner: Jonah) — due 2026-03-10 17:00.
- [ ] Assign 1 engineer for rollback automation MVP (owner: Marcus Li) — due 2026-03-17.
- [ ] Legal to finalize privacy attestation template (owner: Priya Menon) — due 2026-03-15.
- [ ] Update public-facing status note for ACME (owner: comms) — due 2026-03-10 12:00.
- [ ] Post-meeting: add follow-up tickets (serving-runtime backlog) and link to JIRA-RDW-2410 (owner: product ops) — due 2026-03-11.

Notes to self (quick heuristics while facilitating):
- Keep metric slides to max 3; use visuals only if they highlight trend.
- When debate stalls, call a 5-minute asynchronous follow-up and assign a small working group.
- Convert any 'we should explore' to explicit experiment owners and timelines.

Pre-reads to drop (what I will upload 24–48h before):
- One-pager: "Dedicated burst ask — 48h temporary increase" (1 page).
- Incident timeline: last 14 days (bullet list).
- Resource ask: 2 week plan for rollback automation (owner/time/phases).

Follow-up template to paste into Slack / email after the meeting: 
"Thanks everyone — brief recap: decisions: [list], owners: [list + deadlines]. I've created follow-up tickets and will ping owners directly. If you need to change deadlines please reply. — Asha"

Quick personal reminders:
- Bring a printed copy of the one-pager in case screens fail.
- Watch for finance ping after burst approval; be ready to escalate to CFO.
- After meeting: 30m buffer to triage incoming questions and convert notes into Jira tasks.

Scratch area (shorthand ideas / snippets to paste into meeting chat):
- "Short version: approve limited burst -> prevents immediate churn, cost capped, rollback automation is parallel work."
- "We recommend 48h hard window; auto-cut if usage exceeds projected 2x of ACME baseline."
- "If legal sign-off delayed, we proceed with the technical rollback scope and pause customer comms until cleared."

End of preflight.

(Use this doc as ephemeral prep; move final action items into Jira and Confluence after sync.)
